s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive back pain with radiating pain and spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Back pain radiating to the left side
Intradural extramedullary lesion at T8-T9 level
key_facts: 66-year-old female patient
Osteoporosis
Back pain gradually worsening in recent months
Left nephrectomy due to kidney stones about 1 year ago
Taking alendronate 70 mg once a week for osteoporosis
Normal laboratory tests including serum creatinine, calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, thyrotropin and thyroid hormones
Degenerative changes of the vertebral bodies on lumbar spine X-ray
T-scores of both the lumbar spine and proximal femur were less than -3 on dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
35 × 9 mm sized mass occupying the spinal canal at T8-T9 level on MRI
Lesion compressing the spinal cord from posterior with peripheral rim enhancement
Tumor consisted of elongated spindle cells with vesicular nucleus arrayed in a palisade pattern
Neoplastic cells were negative for epithelial membrane antigen, pancytokeratin and desmin but diffuse positive for protein S-100

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Intradural extramedullary lesion with spinal cord compression and peripheral rim enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed intradural extramedullary lesion with hypointense signal on T1-weighted images and heterogene hyperintense signal on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Elongated spindle cells with vesicular nucleus arrayed in a palisade pattern and positive for protein S-100 on immunohistochemical analysis

shortlist.label: Spinal cord lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive back pain with radiating pain and spinal cord compression, although less likely given the histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Spinal hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic areas with peripheral rim enhancement on MRI, although the histopathological findings are not typical for this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The tumor's characteristics, such as being a well-circumscribed intradural extramedullary lesion with spindle cells arrayed in a palisade pattern and diffuse positivity for protein S-100, are consistent with a schwannoma. The lack of epithelial membrane antigen, pancytokeratin, and desmin expression also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas are typically positive for epithelial membrane antigen, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas often have a more disorganized cellular pattern and may contain a mix of cell types, which is not described here.

rejected.label: Spinal cord lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphomas would typically have a more aggressive appearance and different immunohistochemical markers, such as positivity for lymphoid markers.

rejected.label: Spinal hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Hemangioblastomas are typically highly vascular tumors with a distinct appearance on imaging and histology, which does not match the description provided.
